questions.q: Dry sodium propanoate is heated strongly with soda lime. The gaseous hydrocarbon formed is:
questions.explain: Soda-lime decarboxylation is a step-down reaction: the carboxylate carbon leaves as Na₂CO₃, so the C₃ salt gives the C₂ alkane, ethane.

questions.q: Which acid loses CO₂ simply on gentle warming, without soda lime?
questions.explain: A β-keto acid decarboxylates through a six-membered cyclic transition state to give an enol, then acetone. A β-hydroxy acid instead loses water to give CH₃CH=CHCOOH, and simple acids need soda lime.

questions.q: 2,2-Dimethylpropanedioic acid, (CH₃)₂C(COOH)₂, is heated. The organic product is:
questions.explain: In a gem-dicarboxylic (malonic) acid one COOH acts as the β-carbonyl for the other, so only one CO₂ is lost, giving (CH₃)₂CH–COOH.

questions.q: Using the exam convention for β,γ-unsaturated acids, CH₃–CH=CH–CH₂–COOH on heating gives:
questions.explain: The acid H moves to the far alkene carbon through a six-membered cyclic transition state, the double bond shifts and CO₂ leaves, giving CH₃CH₂CH=CH₂. The trap is to keep the C=C in its original position (but-2-ene).
